data.name: Arbaaz
data.gender_notes: Arbaaz is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Arabic, Arbaaz means 'Four' or 'Powerful'. In Islamic history, it is the name of a companion of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) known for his courage and strength. The name Arbaaz carries the meaning “Four, powerful” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Arbaaz usually hope their child will grow to embody four, powerful and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Arbaaz belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Four, powerful.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Arbaaz total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

The name also relates to the four representatives of God's messengers in Islamic theology (Angels).

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya (The Beginning and the End) - Volume 13, pages 263-264 The name Arbaaz carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Arbaaz bin Mansoor Al-Harasi was an Islamic jurist and theologian in the Maghreb. He was born in the city of Sijilmasa (Morocco), and studied under Ibn Ghaylan Al-Maghribi. Arbaaz is known for his book 'Al-Mawasit wal-Mawqif', which was an influential work on the Maliki school of Islamic jurisprudence. He died in 570 AH (1174 AD).

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Abd al-Hadid's Sharh Nahj al-Balagha - Volume 12, page 379 The name Arbaaz carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Arbaaz bin Mansoor Al-Harasi is also mentioned in connection with a famous debate between Imam Al-Haddad and another scholar, Ibn Al-Makhsus. The debate took place in Morocco and is described in detail in Ibn Abd al-Hadid's commentary on Imam Ali's speeches, known as Nahj al-Balagha. Arbaaz was a contemporary of both scholars and acted as a judge in the debate. He is known for his fairness and impartiality in the proceedings.
